page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1108.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 893.0, both placing in the lower tiers. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 11776.53 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5757.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 75.3 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 53.85 GB/sec for large block write operations.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without demanding top-tier single-threaded CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis (achieving 11.19 million SET operations per second in benchmarks), and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks such as software compilation or text processing. It is less optimal for single-threaded compression tasks or heavy LLM inference workloads.
